# apple_subscription_availability (Resource)

Manages the territories an auto-renewable subscription is sold in.

A subscription has exactly one availability record, and it is a **prerequisite for pricing**: until one exists, Apple rejects `apple_subscription_price` with a 409 that mentions only "an error occurred while processing the pricing information" and never names the missing availability. Create this resource before any `apple_subscription_price`, or let Terraform order it for you by referencing the subscription from both.

~> **This resource cannot be destroyed.** Apple publishes neither `PATCH` nor `DELETE` for an availability: a change is a `POST` that supersedes the previous record, and there is no way to return a subscription to having no availability at all. `terraform destroy` drops it from state and warns; the territories remain as last set. To stop selling in a territory, remove it from `available_territories` — that is a normal in-place update.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "apple_apps" "example" {
  bundle_id = "com.example.app"
}

resource "apple_subscription_group" "premium" {
  app_id         = data.apple_apps.example.apps[0].id
  reference_name = "Premium"
}

resource "apple_subscription" "pro_monthly" {
  group_id            = apple_subscription_group.premium.id
  product_id          = "com.example.app.pro.monthly"
  name                = "Pro Monthly"
  subscription_period = "ONE_MONTH"
}

# A subscription has exactly one availability record, and it is a prerequisite
# for pricing: until one exists, Apple rejects apple_subscription_price with a
# 409 that mentions only "an error occurred while processing the pricing
# information" and never names the missing availability.
#
# Territories are named by three-letter Apple code -- USA, GBR, EGY -- not by
# the two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.
#
# This resource cannot be destroyed: Apple publishes neither PATCH nor DELETE
# for an availability, so an update is a POST that supersedes the previous
# record, and terraform destroy drops it from state and warns. To stop selling
# in a territory, remove it from available_territories.
resource "apple_subscription_availability" "pro_monthly" {
  subscription_id              = apple_subscription.pro_monthly.id
  available_in_new_territories = true

  available_territories = [
    "USA",
    "GBR",
    "DEU",
    "FRA",
    "EGY",
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `available_territories` (Set of String) The three-letter Apple territory codes the subscription is sold in, for example `["USA", "GBR", "EGY"]`. A set, because Apple returns them in no particular order. At least one is required, and a territory must be listed here before an `apple_subscription_price` can name a price point in it.
- `subscription_id` (String) The ID of the `apple_subscription` whose availability this is. Cannot be changed after creation.

### Optional

- `available_in_new_territories` (Boolean) Whether the subscription is offered automatically in territories the App Store adds in future. Defaults to `true`, matching App Store Connect's own default. Set it to `false` to keep the territory list exactly as configured.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The unique Apple-generated identifier for the availability record. Apple issues a new one every time availability is replaced.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# The import ID is the subscription ID, not the availability ID: a subscription
# has exactly one availability record, and Apple publishes no collection of them
# to look one up in.
terraform import apple_subscription_availability.pro_monthly 6739472901
```
